record.paper_title: PURE O-SEQUENCES: KNOWN RESULTS, APPLICATIONS AND OPEN PROBLEMS
record.original_question: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4, 5, 21)? Equivalently, is the sequence (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) a pure O-sequence?

evidence.quote: The smallest value of r for which the existence of S(4, 5, r) is currently open is 21. In other words, it is unknown whether (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197) is a pure O-sequence.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Steiner system S(t,k,v) is a pair (X, B), where X is a set of v points and B is a collection of k-element subsets of X (called blocks), such that every t-element subset of X is contained in exactly one block of B. A Steiner quintuple system of order v is a Steiner system S(4,5,v).

A finite sequence h = (h_0, h_1, ..., h_e) of nonnegative integers is called a pure O-sequence if there exists a finite, nonempty set M of monomials in some polynomial ring k[x_1, ..., x_n] (over a field k) such that:
(i) M is an order ideal, i.e., whenever a monomial m lies in M, every monomial dividing m also lies in M;
(ii) all maximal monomials of M (with respect to divisibility) have the same total degree e; and
(iii) for each i = 0, 1, ..., e, h_i equals the number of monomials in M of total degree i.

Question: Does there exist a Steiner quintuple system S(4,5,21)? Equivalently, is the integer sequence
   (1, 21, 210, 1330, 5985, 1197)
a pure O-sequence?
artifact.status_search_result: The existence of a Steiner system S(4,5,21) is the smallest open case for Steiner quintuple systems. Partial results restrict the possible automorphism group orders of such a system to {1,2,3,4,5,6,7,10} (Kolotoğlu, J. Combin. Designs, 2014), but no construction or non-existence proof has been published as of 2026. Recent surveys and references continue to list it as open.

status_evidence.title: Steiner system - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: The smallest order for which the existence of S(4,5,v) is unknown is v = 21.
status_evidence.claim: S(4,5,21) is the smallest open case for Steiner quintuple systems.

status_evidence.title: On the Possible Automorphism Groups of a Steiner Quintuple System of Order 21
status_evidence.snippet: If an S(4,5,21) exists, the order of its full automorphism group is 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, or 10.
status_evidence.claim: Partial structural restrictions are known, but existence is not resolved.
